title: Redwood Security Review - SSO/SCIM & RBAC Deep Dive
summary: Redwood team walked Acme through SSO/SAML setup options (IdP metadata, certificate rotation), SCIM provisioning (user/group sync, attribute mappings), and RBAC recommendations for least-privilege. Customer concerns: SCIM bulk provisioning, group filtering, certificate rotation cadence, service account hardening, and audit log retention for SOC 2. Agreed next steps: share SSO setup guide, SCIM mapping example, RBAC role matrix, and schedule a follow-up pilot window for SAML test and SCIM sync in their dev environment.
topics: SAML SSO: IdP metadata, SP metadata, cert rotation
SCIM provisioning: users, groups, attribute mappings, bulk sync
RBAC: Admin/Dev/Viewer roles, least-privilege, service accounts
Data residency and private deployment considerations
questions: Can we use Okta as IdP and have SCIM push groups?
How often does Redwood rotate SAML certificates and what is the rollover process?
Can we limit SCIM to a subset of groups or OUs?
How are service accounts scoped and audited?
What's the audit log retention and export format for compliance?
Is customer-managed KMS supported in Private deployments?
action_items: Ravi Patel: Share SSO quickstart guide + sample IdP metadata (due: 2025-08-12)
Lena Ortiz: Provide SCIM attribute mapping example and group-filtering docs (due: 2025-08-14)
Maya Chen: Send proposed RBAC role matrix and recommended least-priv access policy (due: 2025-08-11)
Marcus Lee (Acme): Provision test Okta org and invite Redwood test SP account (due: 2025-08-18)
Samir Khan (Acme): Confirm audit log retention requirement (30/90/365 days) and share SOC 2 scope doc (due: 2025-08-13)
next_steps: Redwood to send SSO/SCIM docs and RBAC matrix
Customer to spin up test Okta and share metadata for a SAML test
Schedule 60-min follow-up for SAML handoff and SCIM first-sync (target week of 2025-08-18)
Agree on audit log retention window and export format for SOC 2 evidence
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-07
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel, Lena Ortiz (Redwood); Jillian Park, Marcus Lee, Samir Khan (Acme Financial)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros and then jump into the SSO and RBAC items we agreed on.
[00:18] Jillian: thanks. I'm Jillian; CISO at Acme, joining with Marcus and Samir. Our goal today is to understand how Redwood will fit into our IdP model and compliance requirements, and validate we can do least-privilege RBAC and SCIM provisioning.
[00:35] Ravi: great, yeah we'll run through SAML flow, SSO metadata, SCIM provision, and then lena will go into audit and RBAC specifics.
[00:46] Marcus: quick note, we're on Okta for IdP, using groups mapped from AD via Okta, so group sync and filtering is pretty important for us.
[00:58] Lena: totally understood — we support Okta, Auth0, GCI and any SAML2-compliant IdP; for SCIM we use the standard /Users and /Groups endpoints, with group filtering available via attribute filters or a whitelist on the SP side.
[01:18] Samir: when you say whitelist on the SP side, do you mean Redwood can be configured to ignore certain SCIM group pushes?
[01:24] Lena: yes, exactly. You can configure SCIM to only accept groups that match regex or a provided group list. It's in the SCIM settings in Console, and we can provide a sample mapping.
[01:36] Marcus: that's helpful — we have segmentation rules, so we'd only like specific AD OUs to be provisioned.
[01:42] Ravi: ok jumping into the SAML specifics: on our side we expose SP metadata XML which includes ACS URL, entityID, and a signing certificate. Customers upload IdP metadata (xml or url) into the Console.
[01:56] Jillian: what's your certificate rotation cadence? Our security team wants short-lived certs or a clear rollover process.
[02:05] Lena: our default signing certs rotate every 12 months; we support a rollover window where you can upload the new cert and we accept both certs for 48 hours. We can also configure shorter windows for enterprise customers — e.g., 90-day rotation via Managed Private.
[02:23] Samir: do you support key roll for encryption at rest, customer-managed KMS?
[02:29] Ravi: For Hosted we use platform-managed keys by default, but for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and key rotation policies. We documented that in the security whitepaper.
[02:44] Jillian: for SOC 2, we need audit logs and proof of who performed admin actions. What does Redwood capture?
[02:52] Lena: we log admin actions, SAML provisioning events, SCIM sync events, and token usage; logs are exportable in JSON/CSV and we can support 365-day retention as an add-on. We also have immutable audit trails for RBAC changes.
[03:08] Marcus: is there an API to pull logs into our SIEM?
[03:12] Ravi: yes we expose a logs API with cursor-based pagination; many customers pipe logs to Splunk/CloudWatch via our export connector.
[03:21] Jillian: back to SCIM: what about initial bulk provisioning? We have 12k users and several hundred groups — will the provisioning time out?
[03:30] Lena: SCIM supports bulk operations but depends on IdP push behavior. We recommend doing a staged sync: initial one-time full import via CSV + API, then SCIM incremental for day-to-day. We can also throttle provisioning window to avoid spikes.
[03:48] Samir: any gotchas with attribute mappings? We use mail, employeeNumber and department attributes.
[03:54] Ravi: we map mail->email, employeeNumber->external_id, department->group membership if configured. We'll send the sample mapping showing attribute to field translations.
[04:06] (crosstalk) Jillian: when we onboard, will the RBAC roles map to Okta groups automatically?
[04:12] Lena: yes you can map groups to roles (Admin, Developer, Viewer) and additionally assign quotas/route-level permissions. For least-privilege we suggest a default Viewer role, scoped Developer for model/route editing, and Admin for org-level config.
[04:30] Marcus: what about service accounts for automation — how do you recommend scoping them?
[04:35] Ravi: service accounts are scoped to a project or route; tokens can be restricted by route, model, and TTL. We recommend short TTLs, use of per-project service accounts, and limiting token creation to Admins only.
[04:50] Samir: do we get visibility when a service account is used?
[04:53] Lena: yes, service account usage is logged with actor, IP, and token id, and is included in the audit export.
[04:59] Jillian: for SOC 2 evidence we also need configuration change history — e.g., changes to RBAC mappings or SSO config. Is that retained?
[05:07] Lena: yes we retain configuration history, who changed what, and you can pull timeline entries for the period requested. This is part of our audit logs package.
[05:18] Marcus: what about SCIM failures — do you surface error reasons per user sync?
[05:23] Ravi: SCIM sync failures return per-user error codes and we surface them in Console with a retry queue; we'll also send you the failure codes mapping.
[05:34] Jillian: any limitations on group nesting? Our Okta groups are nested heavily.
[05:40] Lena: we flatten nested groups for provisioned groups; you can choose to preserve hierarchy by prefixing group names. Deep nesting can impact sync performance, we recommend limiting to 2 levels for production.
[05:53] Marcus: network-wise, do you support IP allowlisting or SAML connections via private link?
[05:58] Ravi: we support IP allowlists for Admin Console and API. For Private deployments we can use VPC peering or PrivateLink for the control/data plane depending on the deployment.
[06:12] Samir: about role separation of duties — can we have an approver flow for new Admins?
[06:18] Lena: we don't have built-in approval workflows today, but you can integrate RBAC with your internal access request system via SCIM group updates and a webhook; we can help design a pattern.
[06:30] Jillian: ok would like to see your RBAC role matrix and minimal permissions for Developer vs Admin.
[06:36] Maya: we'll share a recommended role matrix — with explicit list of permissions per role, and recommendations for service account usage.
[06:43] (typing)
[07:00] Ravi: quick demo — here's the Console SSO config screen, you upload IdP metadata url or xml, configure assertion consumer URL, map attributes. Note: some transcription artifacts, screen share shows ACS URL with /saml/acs and entity id redwood:sso:acme.
[07:20] Marcus: if we use metadata url, do you fetch updates automatically?
[07:24] Lena: we can optionally pull IdP metadata periodically; otherwise we rely on customer to push changes. Auto-pull requires you to allow our metadata fetcher IPs in your IdP.
[07:36] Samir: can SCIM be limited to only sync users from certain OUs?
[07:40] Ravi: yes via Okta filter rules or via SCIM group whitelist. We'll document both approaches.
[07:48] Jillian: encryption at rest — you said hosted uses platform-managed keys. For enterprise, can we bring our own key?
[07:55] Lena: yes, for Private deployments you can use your KMS; for Dedicated we have options to integrate with cloud KMS and rotate keys on your cadence.
[08:06] Marcus: audit log exports — what format and throughput?
[08:10] Ravi: JSON lines over S3 or pushed via webhook; throughput is throttled but sufficient for streaming to SIEM. We provide example ingestion code.
[08:20] Jillian: one last compliance item — where is customer data stored? We need data residency in US-EAST for regulated products.
[08:28] Lena: Hosted supports region pinning; we have region options including us-east1 and eu-west1. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
[08:41] Samir: ok, sounds good.
[08:45] Maya: recap — we'll send SSO quickstart, SCIM mapping, RBAC matrix, and schedule a SAML test in your Okta test org.
[08:54] Jillian: thanks all. We'll aim to have the Okta test org by 2025-08-18.
[09:00] (meeting continues with minor scheduling details and doc links)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution may be off; some product names (e.g., Console URLs) transcribed approximately.
